newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt ends lower, hampered by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: German debt ends lower, hampered by strong dollar.

text.p: Bunds ended afternoon trade on Monday weaker after the relentless rise of the dollar against the mark put pressure on the German debt market.
The September Bund future ended at 102.67 points, down 0.32, off earlier lows of 102.51.
Dealers said earlier in the day that the market would find support at 102.67 and this held in the end, despite slipping earlier. The next level of support at 102.53 points held firm.
Market players went on to say that the market would consolidate further over the next few days, with a further flattening of the yield curve also a possibility.

"The main reason behind the losses was the currency, which particularly hit short- and mid-term contracts," one trader said. He went on to say that he was more optimistic on prospects for coming days.
A U.K. investment bank said that German debt was a little out of fashion at the moment, but on a fundamental basis the market would soon start to pick itself up and rise again.
Dealers said that they expected a trading range of between 102.50 and 103.15 points for the Bund future on Tuesday.
They also said that the market would be keeping a close eye on U.S. retail sales on Tuesday at 1230 GMT.
Other indicators of importance this week included U.S. consumer prices for June, due on Wednesday at 1230 GMT.
